teams.name: Cachasol Cartel

nameHistory.name: C u M C back KIDZ!!!

teams.commentary: Lil Baby released an album called FRESH on Friday, and Mike D. went fresh too: Adonai Mitchell, picked up this week, started immediately and scored a zero. The Cartel lost to Hearn by 1.2 with more than 23 points on the bench, where Audric Estime, the other new arrival, and Dak Prescott, who outscored Jayden Daniels again, could each have won it alone. Mike D. owns the deepest quarterback room in the league and the shakiest instincts about which end of it to use. He stays first because his all-play record is still the best in the league by a distance, but with George Pickens questionable, Terry McLaurin on IR and Tyreek Hill cut, the receivers behind Ja'Marr Chase are Omar Cooper Jr. and a hope, and the first-place team should be shopping.

teams.name: Christopher Dootron
teams.commentary: Druski became the first internet creator to host SNL on Saturday, and Sam, the most prolific content creator on the Fadunkadunk waiver wire, got a headlining slot of his own. Three fresh pickups, Jake Bates, Devin Singletary and the Giants defense, all started and combined for nearly 34 points, with the Giants winning in Philadelphia for the first time in thirteen years. Sam posted the top score of the week, beat all eleven teams in the all-play, left about a point on his bench and jumped four spots to second, a strange address for a roster ranked dead last on draft day. He has made 36 pickups this season, more than anyone by a mile, and the bit is finally working. Bijan looks like Bijan again, and with Omarion Hampton, Jordan Mason and Singletary behind him the backfield is suddenly crowded; the soft spot now is receiver, where Michael Wilson is on IR and Jordan Addison is the next man up.

teams.name: DINO NUGGETS

nameHistory.name: The Man the Myth the Legend

teams.commentary: Baker once named his team Feed the Beast, and on Sunday the beast went hungry: Jahmyr Gibbs, the $71 keeper, managed about half his projection, Justin Jefferson scored 7.3, and Trevor Lawrence never got going. The Dino Nuggets won anyway, with the ninth-best score of the week, because Foy brought the worst, the kind of win the committee respects about as much as a forfeit. Baker made no moves again and is 6-3 with a losing all-play record, so he is either a genius or asleep at the wheel of a car that keeps arriving on time. ESPN still likes his rest-of-season roster more than anyone's, and with six receivers and only Rico Dowdle behind Gibbs and Chuba Hubbard, the trade writes itself: a Xavier Worthy or Keon Coleman for a running back.

teams.name: Ammonia Coladas
teams.commentary: Godzilla Minus Zero topped the box office this weekend, and Mark's defense went one better: minus five. He started the Patriots, ranked 11th of 12 defenses by projection, on the day Green Bay put up the most points New England has ever allowed at Gillette, and that wasn't even his worst decision. Josh Jacobs, now listed OUT, started at running back and scored half a point, the bust of the week. Frum, of all people, beat the Coladas by nearly 25, and Mark slid two spots to fourth. The backfield is a waiting room, with Jacobs and Kyle Monangai out and Brian Robinson Jr. on IR, leaving Bucky Irving, Kenny Gainwell and Chris Rodriguez Jr.: plenty of bodies, not much depth.

teams.name: $200 Dolla Holla
teams.commentary: Notre Dame knocked off No. 1 Miami on Saturday, and Hearn did the same to the first-place Cartel on Sunday, by 1.2, with a lineup that left less than a point on the bench. Christian Watson and Brock Purdy both cleared 25, and Evan McPherson kicked in 13, which in a one-point game is the whole margin and then some. D'Andre Swift, flagged as his worst pick on draft day, scored about 3, so August got one right too. Fittingly for the Dolla Holla, beating the top team still cost him a spot, because Sam jumped everybody. The owner of the second-best all-play record in the league has a running back problem nobody is talking about: behind Cook and Swift the only other back is Ray Davis, while Devaughn Vele, Antonio Williams and two questionable veterans give him receivers to spare.

teams.name: Papas McButt Nuggets

nameHistory.name: Why dont you just call them?

teams.commentary: Jordan Love threw for 372 yards in Foxborough and Jordan got 36 points out of it, the best quarterback day in any lineup, and Jordan still lost. The McButt Nuggets posted the fourth-best total of the week and fell to Sam by five while the 49ers defense put up 19 on the bench behind the Browns' 8, an 11-point swing in a five-point loss. Jordan has now left nearly 200 points on his bench this season, about 40 more than anyone else, which is less a pattern than a lifestyle. Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Jonathan Taylor both scored under half their projections, and with Rhamondre Stevenson doubtful and Garrett Wilson questionable, Jordan has backs to sell in Tyler Allgeier and Seth McGowan and receivers to buy.

teams.name: Captain Casper's Low Risk Tacos

nameHistory.name: Coach Matty Ps D In Swishs V

teams.commentary: Danny once named his team We Coming for T Swish, and on Sunday he finally arrived: Los Desperados beat the reigning champ by nearly 35, the biggest margin of the week. Brett scored 86.5, tenth-best, with Josh Allen held to 12.7 in Monday night's win over Minnesota and Saquon Barkley and Aaron Jones combining for about 11. The kicker call went sideways too, Ka'imi Fairbairn scoring 17 on the bench while Tyler Bass started, and C.J. Stroud, whom Brett cut this week, threw five touchdowns for Houston on Sunday for nobody's fantasy team. The Low Risk Tacos turned out to be low reward, and they fell two spots to seventh. Jaylen Warren returns from the Steelers' bye to a backfield with plenty of bodies, but with DeVonta Smith out, the receivers after Chris Olave are Keenan Allen, Ryan Flournoy and a waiver claim.

teams.name: Quintosss... Amigo?
teams.commentary: The Amigos beat Hess by 5.8 with the eighth-best score of the week, the kind of win you don't frame. Jeff swapped Chris Boswell for Cairo Santos and got the exact same 9 points, a lateral move executed with surgical precision. Brock Bowers carried the lineup, Quinshon Judkins managed 5 on a projection over 13, and Breece Hall outscored Braelon Allen from the bench, a swing that happened to equal the entire margin of victory. Jeff still sets the most efficient lineups in the league, which is why he climbs to eighth, and with Tony Pollard back from the Titans' bye he has four healthy backs. That makes the Amigos one of the few teams with a running back to sell, and Hall or Allen should be on the phone to Baker or Hearn.

teams.name: Table Shepherds McPie

nameHistory.name: your son rip  on line toot
Fernet and The Music Hall Mack

teams.commentary: The Table Shepherds set the table for Baker. Foy posted the lowest score of the week, lost to all eleven teams in the all-play, and authored the bench bomb of the week for good measure: Ladd McConkey, the $18 keeper, started through a questionable tag and scored a zero while Courtland Sutton, Danny's castoff, scored 13 on the bench, enough to flip an 11.5-point loss by himself. Jared Goff added 5.3 on a day he threw for a season-low 170 yards, and the new kicker, Jason Myers, kicked 6, so the kicker saga continues even now that there's a kicker. The backfield is the one deep spot on the roster, with Jonah Coleman, Blake Corum and Dylan Sampson behind Kyren Williams, while two receivers are on IR and McConkey is questionable, so Foy needs a back-for-receiver deal more than anyone in the league.

teams.name: Los Desperados Sudados
teams.commentary: Tennessee beat No. 6 Kentucky by 28 on Saturday, and Danny staged his own rout on Sunday, beating the reigning champ by nearly 35 with the second-best score of the week. CeeDee Lamb, Joe Burrow and Matthew Golden all cleared 27, and for once the bench had no say in the result, though Rome Odunze's 14 did sit behind DJ Moore's 5. Danny is 3-6 with the third-best all-play record in the league and still the worst luck number, so the committee holds him at tenth with genuine sympathy. He also picked up Alvin Kamara after Frum cut him, which gives Los Desperados backs to burn behind Ashton Jeanty and Chase Brown with Travis Etienne and RJ Harvey on IR. With spare receivers too, a team two games out of the playoff line should be turning depth into points this week.

teams.name: Dad Bellies Doin' Salt Smellies

nameHistory.name: Lots of ??? But Tons of Upside!
Poopy Wake Up Call On Line Toot
The Best Butt of the Bunch

teams.commentary: Dad Bellies Doin' Salt Smellies, and for one Sunday the smelling salts worked. Oregon walked into Columbus and beat Ohio State on Saturday, and Frum pulled off his own upset a day later, beating Mark by nearly 25 with the third-best score of the week. Kenneth Walker, the $39 keeper, scored three touchdowns in Kansas City's rout of the Jets and 34.3 for Frum, Bryce Young topped 20, and Spencer Shrader kicked 16, so the Bellies climb out of the basement. The waiver work was mixed: Frum dropped the Commanders defense a week after it scored 14, picked up the Lions, who scored 10, and cut Alvin Kamara, who now lives on Danny's bench. The backfield behind Walker is the deepest in the league, five backs deep even with Cam Skattebo out, while the receivers after Zay Flowers are Denzel Boston and a questionable Jaylen Waddle, so the trade Frum needs has been obvious for six weeks.

teams.name: For Heaven Sakes, Woman
teams.commentary: Hess once called his team Best Available, which would be a fine motto if he ever started it. The Rams defense scored 11 on his bench while the Bengals started and scored 3, and Ryan Fitzgerald kicked 2, so a 5.8-point loss to Jeff was self-inflicted. The receivers did their part: Puka Nacua caught 14 passes for 28 points, and KC Concepcion added nearly 17 on a 64-yard touchdown from Shedeur Sanders. Hess falls to last with the fewest points in the league, and the injury report is the scariest page in the file: Nacua is now listed doubtful, Davante Adams is on IR, and the backs behind Christian McCaffrey are Kimani Vidal and a questionable TreVeyon Henderson. He needs a back and a receiver, and Concepcion and Tre Tucker are the only currency he has.

commentary.intro: Notre Dame knocked off No. 1 Miami on Saturday, and the upset bug reached Fadunkadunk by Monday night: Hearn beat the first-place Cartel by 1.2 with Dak Prescott's winning points sitting on Mike D.'s bench. The Cartel keeps the top spot anyway, but it now has company at 6-3, with Sam, Baker and Mark all tied, and the committee has a new number two. Sam, whose roster was ranked dead last on draft day, posted the top score of the week, beat every team in the all-play and jumped four spots. Baker won with the ninth-best score because Foy brought the worst, and Mark lost to Frum, of all people, after his Patriots defense went negative on the day Green Bay hung the most points New England has ever allowed at home. The reigning champ took the beating of the week, and Jordan lost a five-point game with 19 points of 49ers defense on his bench, which we will get to.

awards.benchBomb: Foy started Ladd McConkey, his $18 keeper, through a questionable tag and got a zero while Courtland Sutton scored 13 on the bench, enough by itself to flip an 11.5-point loss. McConkey has now cost him keeper money and a game.
awards.worstDefense: Godzilla Minus Zero topped the box office this weekend, and Mark's Patriots went minus five, giving up 45 to Green Bay, the most New England has ever allowed at Gillette. They were the 11th-ranked defense of 12 by projection, so nobody can say he wasn't warned.
awards.toughestLoss: Jordan scored 116.9, fourth-best of the week, and lost by 5 with the 49ers defense scoring 19 on his bench behind the Browns' 8. That isn't tough luck. That's a tough read of the lineup screen.
awards.closest: Hearn over Mike D. by 1.2, and Mike D. had three different ways to win it sitting on his bench, starting with Dak Prescott outscoring Jayden Daniels by five.
awards.luckiestWin: Baker won with 87, the ninth-best score of the week, because Foy brought the worst.
awards.highScore: Sam, 121.9, a perfect 11-0 all-play week built on three fresh pickups.
awards.lowScore: Foy, 75.5, and an 0-11 week in the all-play.
awards.blowout: Danny over Brett A. by 34.9, and the Swish holder never really showed up.
awards.boom: Jordan Love threw for 372 yards against New England and scored 36.1 on a projection of 17, the best quarterback day in any lineup.
awards.bust: Josh Jacobs, now listed OUT, scored 0.5 in Mark's lineup on a projection of 14.6.
awards.bestDefense: Sam picked up the Giants, started them, and got 14, the best defensive score of the week, as New York won in Philadelphia for the first time in thirteen years.
awards.questionableStart: Brett A. started Keenan Allen over Ryan Flournoy and lost a couple of points on the call, a rounding error in a 35-point loss.

commentary.outro:
Week 10 headliner: Hearn against Brett A., fifth against seventh, the manager who just beat the first-place team against the reigning champ who just lost by 35. Mark gets Jeff, Jordan gets Danny, and Sam takes his three-pickup lineup to Frum, whose backfield could start for half the league. Mike D. gets Foy, and Baker gets Hess, which is about as close to a bye as a 6-3 team can draw.

Trade Desk: the NFL trade deadline is today, and Fadunkadunk should treat it like its own. Running backs are still the currency, and the sellers are easy to spot. Frum has five healthy backs behind Kenneth Walker and almost nothing at receiver behind Zay Flowers; Hearn has receivers stacked to the ceiling and nobody behind James Cook and D'Andre Swift but Ray Davis. Ollie Gordon II for Devaughn Vele fixes both teams in one phone call. Jordan has Tyler Allgeier and Seth McGowan to spare and needs a receiver; Baker has six receivers and only Rico Dowdle behind his starting backs, so Allgeier for Xavier Worthy works in both directions. Jeff's Breece Hall is the other back on the market, and Foy, with three backs behind Kyren Williams and a receiver room on IR, should be offering Blake Corum to anyone with a wideout. Hess needs everything and has KC Concepcion, which is a start. Move of the week: Sam picking up Jake Bates, Devin Singletary and the Giants defense, starting all three, and getting nearly 34 points in a five-point win. Anti-move of the week: Mike D. picking up Adonai Mitchell, starting him over Omar Cooper Jr., and getting a zero in a 1.2-point loss. Honorable mention to Brett A., who cut C.J. Stroud the week Stroud threw five touchdowns.

Swish Watch: the reigning champ is 5-4 and seventh, with the lowest three-week scoring average of anyone in the committee's top eight and the hardest remaining schedule in the league. The Low Risk Tacos have become a high-risk proposition: Saquon Barkley, flagged as Brett's worst pick on draft day, scored about 8, DeVonta Smith, the $19 keeper, is out, and the best score on the whole roster this week came from a kicker on the bench. The Swish isn't gone yet, but it has started checking where the exits are. Rankings and commentary refresh every Tuesday morning once ESPN finalizes the week.
